correctness.rationale: The mutual-first-pair induction forces adjacent canonical pairs except when an agent demotes the canonical partner beneath the next available label. For odd x=2j−1, the four-person block has exactly one revised stable matching. For even x=2j, the top remaining three agents form a directed preference cycle, forcing a blocking pair in every perfect matching. All other swaps do not newly prefer a candidate over the canonical partner and retain the unique matching. The k−1 fatal swaps among n(n−2) choices give 1/(2n). Independently enumerated all strict one-adjacent-swap profiles and all perfect matchings for n=4,6,8 (fatal counts 1,2,3 and zero multiple-solution cases); source verify.py independently covers n=4,6,8,10. Finite checks corroborate the all-n proof.
